item.title: FastMCP 3.2 Adds AI‑Assisted Search to Calibre Library
item.description:
FastMCP 3.2 Adds AI‑Assisted Search to Calibre Library

FastMCP 3.2 extends Calibre e‑book library with AI‑assisted search, RAG, and agentic workflows.

🔍 Overview

  • AI‑assisted search, Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG), and agentic workflows for Sandra’s 1000+ book library.
  • Exposes 33 portmanteau tools for natural‑language library management.
  • Built into Calibre’s core engine.

🧩 How it works

  • Bridges Calibre e‑book library and AI assistants (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) via the Model Context Protocol.
  • Reads Calibre’s metadata.db directly and indexes metadata for semantic search using LanceDB.
  • Provides Incremental LanceDB RAG Sync and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) hybrid search.
  • Offers a 21‑tool registry and a portmanteau CRUD & Library Health Engine.

⚙️ Key details

  • FastMCP 3.2 Server (port :10720) and WebApp (Next.js 15 on :10721).
  • Calibre GUI + Plugin (Qt6 / PyQt5).
  • FastAPI REST layer with async background workers.
  • CALIBRE CONTENT SERVER (e.g., :8099, http://goliath:8099/ or http://localhost:8080/).
  • Async Python Engine (calibre.srv) and RapydScript SPA (index-generated.html).
  • HTML5 In‑Browser Reader (viewer.js / offline SW) and OPDS Mobile Catalog Feed.
  • Databases: metadata.db (Calibre SQLite catalog), full-text-search.db (FTS5 token index), calibre_mcp_data.db (sidecar extended metadata).
  • Semantic search powered by LanceDB, fastembed (BAAI/bge-small), and Ollama/OpenAI providers.

🚀 Availability

  • Download Calibre MCP_*_x64-setup.exe from Releases, double‑click to launch Calibre MCP.
  • Claude Desktop one‑liner: download calibre‑mcp.mcpb from Releases and install via Settings → MCP Servers → Install from file.
  • After installation, use prompts such as “Find unread sci‑fi books”, “Open a random Banks novel”, or “What’s my library health?”.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides AI‑powered semantic search and natural‑language library management directly within Calibre.
  • Enables RAG and agentic workflows to help users navigate large e‑book collections efficiently.

#Calibre #AI #LanceDB #SemanticSearch #Python

Source: sandraschi/calibremcp

item.title: AI Usage Tracker: Local-First, Privacy-Focused Tool for Tracking AI Coding Costs
item.description:
AI Usage Tracker: Local-First, Privacy-Focused Tool for Tracking AI Coding Costs

AI Usage Tracker, formerly Claude Usage Tracker, is a local-first tool that automatically discovers and aggregates your AI coding usage across 10+ development tools — covering both Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex.

🔍 Overview

It scans known data directories, parses JSONL/log files, calculates costs using model-specific pricing, and presents everything in a beautiful dark-themed interactive dashboard powered by Chart.js.

🧩 How it works

  • Auto‑discovery detects Claude and Codex tools.
  • Parses JSONL/log files from supported tools.
  • Calculates costs per token using model‑specific pricing.
  • Displays top‑level stats (Today / Week / Month / All‑time / Sessions).

⚙️ Key details

  • Top‑level All / Claude / Codex pill toggle scopes entire dashboard to a single provider.
  • No cloud, no telemetry, no accounts; everything stays on your machine.
  • Cost grouped by working directory to show which projects burn through token budget.
  • Filters by source, model, date range, and minimum cost.
  • Day‑by‑day session timeline with expandable rows and color‑coded model chips.
  • Hourly × day activity grid revealing most productive and expensive coding hours.
  • Drill into any session: token breakdown, conversation preview, one‑click resume command (claude –resume / codex resume ).

#AIUsage #Privacy #DeveloperTools #CostTracking

Source: 658jjh/claude-usage-tracker Source: mostly-ai/mostlyai

item.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 supports LLM inference across hardware
item.description:
llama.cpp v1.0.0 supports LLM inference across hardware

llama.cpp is a C/C++ project for LLM and MLLM inference, with v1.0.0 listed. Its stated goal is to enable inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of hardware, locally and in the cloud.

🔍 Overview

The project is built on the ggml library. It lists Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF among its model references, as well as text-to-speech (TTS) models and GBNF grammars.

⚙️ Usage

After installation, the provided command to run Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF is:

1

llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF

The project also provides a command to launch an OpenAI-compatible API server:

1

llama serve -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF

The listed interfaces include the llama-server REST API and the lib llama API.

🚀 Availability

Installation options listed for llama.cpp include:

  • Visit https://llama.app and follow the instructions.
  • Run with Docker, using the Docker documentation.
  • Download pre-built binaries from the releases page.
  • Build from source by cloning the repository and following the build guide.

The project lists Docker, Winget, Nightly, Server, Release, and an MIT license.

🤝 Contributing

Contributors can open PRs. Collaborators are invited based on contributions, and maintainers can push to branches in the llama.cpp repo and merge PRs into the master branch. The project points contributors to CONTRIBUTING.md for more information.

#llama.cpp #LLMInference #C++ #GGUF

Source: ggml-org/llama.cpp

item.title: TabPFN-TS Brings Zero-Shot Forecasting to Tabular Foundation Models
item.description:
TabPFN-TS Brings Zero-Shot Forecasting to Tabular Foundation Models

TabPFN-TS frames univariate time-series forecasting as tabular regression, using TabPFN and lightweight feature engineering to produce point and probabilistic forecasts. Its paper was accepted to the NeurIPS 2024 TRL and TSALM workshops, and the package’s v1.3.0 release uses TabPFN-3.5 by default.

🔍 Overview

The method transforms a time series into a table, adds engineered features, runs regression with TabPFN, and uses the regression results as forecasts. Multivariate targets are handled as N independent univariate forecasts.

The work reports performance on par with top-tier models across both GIFT-EVAL metrics, and TabPFN-TS is ranked first on the GIFT-EVAL benchmark. The paper is available in a newer version, and the project released v1.0.0 with AutoSeasonalFeatures and improved CalendarFeatures.

🧩 How it works

TabPFN-TS treats forecasting as univariate regression using target history and known-future covariates. It supports zero-shot forecasting without training, as well as point and probabilistic forecasts.

Input or feature How TabPFN-TS handles it
Known dynamic covariates, such as holidays Supported when future values are supplied in future_df. Numeric and boolean covariates also receive lag and trailing-mean features.
Past dynamic covariates, such as weather observations Dropped because future values are unavailable.
Static covariates, such as item ID or store size Currently dropped.
Engineered temporal features, such as calendar and sin/cos features Automatically generated by TABPFN_TS_DEFAULT_FEATURES.

KnownCovariateLagFeature, the first feature in TABPFN_TS_DEFAULT_FEATURES, adds three columns for each numeric or boolean known covariate: lag 1, lag at the season length, and a trailing mean over one season. Season length comes from the timestamp frequency. Features are computed per series over the context and horizon, and horizon rows use covariate values rather than the target.

On 25 fev-bench tasks with numeric known covariates, this feature lowers SQL by 4.5% on the default v3.5 model: 21 of 25 tasks improved, while the worst task increased by 1.5%. The largest gains were on temperature-driven load forecasting.

⚙️ Models and availability

  • As of v1.3.0, TabPFN-3.5 is the default in both LOCAL and CLIENT mode. This model is pretrained purely on synthetic data. The defaults require tabpfn>=9.0.0 and tabpfn-client>=0.5.3.
  • The finetuned TabPFN-TS-3 checkpoint from the TabPFN-3 report remains available. Earlier defaults shipped this checkpoint and required tabpfn>=8.0.0.
  • tabpfn-client is included as the default engine, allowing fast inference without requiring a user’s own GPU.
  • Install the package with pip install tabpfn-time-series.

#TimeSeries #TabPFN #Forecasting #MachineLearning

Source: PriorLabs/tabpfn-time-series

item.title: Microsoft Ends Copilot Support on LG and Samsung Smart TVs
item.description:
Microsoft Ends Copilot Support on LG and Samsung Smart TVs

Microsoft announced that it will discontinue the Copilot AI assistant on all smart TVs, including the LG and Samsung models that launched with the feature at CES 2025.

🔍 Overview

  • Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs.
  • The decision affects LG and Samsung TVs that received Copilot access in 2025.
  • The information originated from an on‑screen notification on a webOS‑powered LG TV, not from an official press release.

🗓️ Timeline

  • CES 2025: LG and Samsung announced new smart TVs with built‑in Microsoft Copilot.
  • December 2025: LG added an unremovable Copilot shortcut to its webOS, prompting user backlash.
  • Early 2026: LG allowed the shortcut to be deleted after user complaints.
  • 2026 (scheduled): Copilot functionality is slated for discontinuation on all TVs; the exact date is “subject to Microsoft’s timeline.”

🤖 What Copilot Did on TVs

  • Acted as an AI‑powered companion that users could chat with.
  • Answered questions about the current screen content.
  • Provided recommendations for TV shows and movies.

⚙️ Why the Change

  • Earlier in 2026, Microsoft launched a new Copilot “super app” that bundles chat, agents, and coding tools.
  • The super app shifts Copilot’s focus toward business and productivity uses rather than a digital companion on consumer devices.

📣 Current Status

  • A notification on LG TVs states: “the Copilot‑enabled feature on your TV is no longer available and may stop functioning shortly.”
  • No exact shutdown date has been provided; the feature is scheduled for discontinuation during 2026.

The discontinuation marks the end of the first generation of AI assistants embedded in mainstream smart TV platforms.

#Microsoft #Copilot #SmartTV #AI

Source: Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs

item.title: Google launches AI Edge Foresight, an offline‑only note‑taking app for macOS
item.description:
Google launches AI Edge Foresight, an offline‑only note‑taking app for macOS

Google has released an experimental note‑taking app called Google AI Edge Foresight that can transcribe meetings and audio files entirely offline.

🔍 Overview

  • Experimental app, free to use
  • Runs on macOS using Google’s on‑device EmbeddingGemma 2 model
  • Transcribes meetings completely offline

🧩 How it works

  • Audio is processed by an on‑device model; no cloud connection is required
  • The model runs locally on Macs with Apple Silicon

⚙️ Features

  • Offline transcription of meetings and audio files
  • Summarizes meetings while providing a space for personal notes, similar to Granola and Wispr Flow
  • Turns shorthand bullet points entered during a meeting into polished notes based on the transcript
  • Built‑in assistant lets you ask questions about the content you heard
  • Ability to connect local files for the assistant to reference when answering questions
  • Files, meeting audio, and notes never leave your computer

🚀 Availability

  • Free to use
  • Optimized for macOS on Apple Silicon Macs only

💡 Why it matters

  • Operates entirely on‑device, keeping data private
  • Provides a privacy‑focused alternative in the growing AI note‑taking market

#Google #AI #NoteTaking #macOS #Privacy

Source: Google’s AI note-taking app transcribes your meetings completely offline
